```typescript
public readonly applicationGithubRepoId: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* unset; only the name-based subject is trusted

`S3` source only: numeric repository ID of the application repository.

Used
with `githubOrgId` to also trust the immutable-ID OIDC trust subject. See
`githubOrgId`.

---

##### `applicationRepositoryName`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="applicationRepositoryName" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.applicationRepositoryName"></a>

```typescript
public readonly applicationRepositoryName: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* 'application'

CodeCommit repository holding the application, cloned into the build context.

---

##### `branchNameParameterName`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="branchNameParameterName" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.branchNameParameterName"></a>

```typescript
public readonly branchNameParameterName: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* '/pipeline/parameters/branchName'

SSM parameter holding the branch both repositories are deployed from.

Only read for the CodeCommit source.

---

##### `githubOrgId`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="githubOrgId" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.githubOrgId"></a>

```typescript
public readonly githubOrgId: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* unset; only the name-based subject is trusted

`S3` source only: the GitHub organization's numeric ID.

Set this together
with `infrastructureGithubRepoId` and `applicationGithubRepoId` when a
repository has "Use repository and organization IDs in the OIDC subject
claim" enabled. GitHub then mints an immutable-ID subject
`repo:<owner>@<orgId>/<repo>@<repoId>:environment:<name>` instead of the
name-based `repo:<owner/repo>:...`.

This setting is per-REPOSITORY, so the two source repos may mint different
forms. When the IDs are set the trust policy trusts BOTH the name-based and
the ID-based subject for every repo, so it is correct whichever form each
repo produces and keeps working if the setting is toggled later. All three
ID fields must be set together; if any is missing only the name-based
subject is trusted.

---

##### `infrastructureGithubRepo`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="infrastructureGithubRepo" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.infrastructureGithubRepo"></a>

```typescript
public readonly infrastructureGithubRepo: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* required for the S3 source

`S3` source only: GitHub `owner/repo` of the infrastructure repository, used in the OIDC trust subject so only its CI can upload the infrastructure source.

Required when `sourceType` is `S3`.

---

##### `infrastructureGithubRepoId`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="infrastructureGithubRepoId" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.infrastructureGithubRepoId"></a>

```typescript
public readonly infrastructureGithubRepoId: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* unset; only the name-based subject is trusted

`S3` source only: numeric repository ID of the infrastructure repository.

Used with `githubOrgId` to also trust the immutable-ID OIDC trust subject.
See `githubOrgId`.

---

##### `infrastructureRepositoryName`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="infrastructureRepositoryName" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.infrastructureRepositoryName"></a>

```typescript
public readonly infrastructureRepositoryName: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* 'infrastructure'

CodeCommit repository holding the infrastructure code.

---

##### `sourceBranch`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="sourceBranch" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.sourceBranch"></a>

```typescript
public readonly sourceBranch: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* 'prod'

`S3` source only: the git branch CI uploads from, allowed to assume the OIDC upload role (`refs/heads/<sourceBranch>` in the trust subject).

Only read when `sourceEnvironment` is unset: a workflow job scoped to a
GitHub Environment mints an `environment:<name>` subject, not a branch one.

---

##### `sourceEnvironment`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="sourceEnvironment" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.sourceEnvironment"></a>

```typescript
public readonly sourceEnvironment: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* unset; the trust uses the branch form with `sourceBranch`

`S3` source only: the name of the GitHub Environment whose OIDC token may assume the upload role.

When set, the trust subject matches
`repo:<owner/repo>:environment:<name>` for both repositories instead of the
branch form `repo:<owner/repo>:ref:refs/heads/<sourceBranch>`.

A GitHub Actions job that declares `environment: <name>` mints an OIDC
token whose `sub` claim is `repo:<owner/repo>:environment:<name>`, so this
must be set (and match the GitHub Environment name) whenever the upload
workflow runs under an environment — otherwise AssumeRole is denied. Set it
to put the GitHub variables inside that environment rather than at the
repository scope.

---

##### `sourceType`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="sourceType" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.sourceType"></a>

```typescript
public readonly sourceType: PipelineSourceType;
```

- *Type:* <a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSourceType">PipelineSourceType</a>
- *Default:* PipelineSourceType.CODECOMMIT

Where the pipeline reads its source from.

`CODECOMMIT` keeps the original behaviour: the infrastructure and
application CodeCommit repositories, on the branch read from
`branchNameParameterName`.

`S3` instead creates two versioned S3 buckets (one for the infrastructure
source, one for the application), an IAM role GitHub Actions assumes over
OIDC to upload `source.zip` into them, and EventBridge rules that start the
pipeline on every upload. The remaining `S3`-only fields configure the OIDC
trust. The OIDC provider itself must already exist in the account.

---

##### `useRepositoryCdkCli`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="useRepositoryCdkCli" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSettings.property.useRepositoryCdkCli"></a>

```typescript
public readonly useRepositoryCdkCli: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false - global install, as before

Runs the synth with the repository's own CDK CLI (`npx cdk`, the `aws-cdk` devDependency installed by `npm ci`) instead of a global `npm install -g aws-cdk` of whatever version is current that day.

The
repository must list `aws-cdk` in its devDependencies.

---

### RdsBootstrapSettings <a name="RdsBootstrapSettings" id="tm-cdk-constructs.RdsBootstrapSettings"></a>

Database bootstrap settings (opt-in).

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="tm-cdk-constructs.RdsBootstrapSettings.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { RdsBootstrapSettings } from 'tm-cdk-constructs'

const rdsBootstrapSettings: RdsBootstrapSettings = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.RdsBootstrapSettings.property.enabled">enabled</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Enables the bootstrap: a VPC Lambda creates the application database and user, sets the user's password from the CDK-generated secret, and imports the dump (`db/latest.sql`) from the bootstrap-assets bucket. Idempotent, and a no-op on stack delete (data retained). Off by default, so other consumers are untouched. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.RdsBootstrapSettings.property.dumpKey">dumpKey</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Key of the dump object in the bootstrap-assets bucket. |

---

##### `enabled`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="enabled" id="tm-cdk-constructs.RdsBootstrapSettings.property.enabled"></a>

```typescript
public readonly enabled: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean

Enables the bootstrap: a VPC Lambda creates the application database and user, sets the user's password from the CDK-generated secret, and imports the dump (`db/latest.sql`) from the bootstrap-assets bucket. Idempotent, and a no-op on stack delete (data retained). Off by default, so other consumers are untouched.

The dump is REQUIRED when enabled: a greenfield TYPO3 against an empty
schema fails every request and the ALB health check never passes, so a
missing dump makes the Lambda fail fast with a clear message rather than a
ten-minute health-check timeout.

---

##### `dumpKey`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="dumpKey" id="tm-cdk-constructs.RdsBootstrapSettings.property.dumpKey"></a>

```typescript
public readonly dumpKey: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* 'db/latest.sql'

Key of the dump object in the bootstrap-assets bucket.

---

##### `cpu`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="cpu" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmApplicationLoadBalancedFargateServiceProps.property.cpu"></a>

```typescript
public readonly cpu: number;
```

- *Type:* number
- *Default:* 256

The number of cpu units used by the task.

Valid values, which determines your range of valid values for the memory parameter:

256 (.25 vCPU) - Available memory values: 0.5GB, 1GB, 2GB

512 (.5 vCPU) - Available memory values: 1GB, 2GB, 3GB, 4GB

1024 (1 vCPU) - Available memory values: 2GB, 3GB, 4GB, 5GB, 6GB, 7GB, 8GB

2048 (2 vCPU) - Available memory values: Between 4GB and 16GB in 1GB increments

4096 (4 vCPU) - Available memory values: Between 8GB and 30GB in 1GB increments

8192 (8 vCPU) - Available memory values: Between 16GB and 60GB in 4GB increments

16384 (16 vCPU) - Available memory values: Between 32GB and 120GB in 8GB increments

This default is set in the underlying FargateTaskDefinition construct.

---

##### `ephemeralStorageGiB`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="ephemeralStorageGiB" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmApplicationLoadBalancedFargateServiceProps.property.ephemeralStorageGiB"></a>

```typescript
public readonly ephemeralStorageGiB: number;
```

- *Type:* number
- *Default:* Undefined, in which case, the task will receive 20GiB ephemeral storage.

The amount (in GiB) of ephemeral storage to be allocated to the task.

The minimum supported value is `21` GiB and the maximum supported value is `200` GiB.

Only supported in Fargate platform version 1.4.0 or later.

---

##### `memoryLimitMiB`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="memoryLimitMiB" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmApplicationLoadBalancedFargateServiceProps.property.memoryLimitMiB"></a>

```typescript
public readonly memoryLimitMiB: number;
```

- *Type:* number
- *Default:* 512

The amount (in MiB) of memory used by the task.

This field is required and you must use one of the following values, which determines your range of valid values
for the cpu parameter:

512 (0.5 GB), 1024 (1 GB), 2048 (2 GB) - Available cpu values: 256 (.25 vCPU)

1024 (1 GB), 2048 (2 GB), 3072 (3 GB), 4096 (4 GB) - Available cpu values: 512 (.5 vCPU)

2048 (2 GB), 3072 (3 GB), 4096 (4 GB), 5120 (5 GB), 6144 (6 GB), 7168 (7 GB), 8192 (8 GB) - Available cpu values: 1024 (1 vCPU)

Between 4096 (4 GB) and 16384 (16 GB) in increments of 1024 (1 GB) - Available cpu values: 2048 (2 vCPU)

Between 8192 (8 GB) and 30720 (30 GB) in increments of 1024 (1 GB) - Available cpu values: 4096 (4 vCPU)

Between 16384 (16 GB) and 61440 (60 GB) in increments of 4096 (4 GB) - Available cpu values: 8192 (8 vCPU)

Between 32768 (32 GB) and 122880 (120 GB) in increments of 8192 (8 GB) - Available cpu values: 16384 (16 vCPU)

This default is set in the underlying FargateTaskDefinition construct.

---

##### `disableDefaultScaling`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="disableDefaultScaling" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmApplicationLoadBalancedFargateServiceProps.property.disableDefaultScaling"></a>

```typescript
public readonly disableDefaultScaling: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false - the built-in CPU + memory target-tracking policies apply.

Completely disable the built-in auto-scaling policies.

By default this construct enables target-tracking auto scaling on both CPU
and memory utilization (targets from `targetCpuUtilizationPercent` /
`targetMemoryUtilizationPercent`, 60-second scale-in/scale-out cooldowns,
capacity from `minTaskCount` / `maxTaskCount`). See
`disableMemoryScaling` to keep only the CPU policy.

Set this to `true` to skip those default policies entirely and take full
control of scaling yourself. The construct still creates the
`ScalableTaskCount` (with the `minTaskCount` / `maxTaskCount` capacity
bounds) and exposes it as {@link scalableTaskCount }, so you can attach any
scaling policy you want (custom CPU/memory targets, request-count scaling,
scheduled scaling, step scaling, ...) from your own stack.

This keeps the current behavior as the default for everyone who does not
pass it, while allowing a complete override.

---

##### `disableMemoryScaling`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="disableMemoryScaling" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmApplicationLoadBalancedFargateServiceProps.property.disableMemoryScaling"></a>

```typescript
public readonly disableMemoryScaling: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Skips the built-in memory target-tracking policy and keeps the CPU one.

A PHP-FPM task's memory utilization is roughly constant whatever the
load, so a memory target either never triggers or scales out to
`maxTaskCount` and stays there. Off by default: existing consumers keep
both policies.

---

##### `monitoringConfiguration`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="monitoringConfiguration" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmApplicationLoadBalancedFargateServiceProps.property.monitoringConfiguration"></a>

```typescript
public readonly monitoringConfiguration: MonitoringConfigurationProperty;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_ecs.CfnService.MonitoringConfigurationProperty
- *Default:* { metricConfigurations: [{ metricNames: ['CPUUtilization'], resolutionSeconds: 20 }] }

The CloudWatch monitoring configuration applied to the ECS service, which controls the resolution of the service-level `CPUUtilization` and `MemoryUtilization` metrics.

By default this construct enables high-resolution (20-second) collection of
the `CPUUtilization` metric, so that target-tracking auto scaling can react
faster. Pass this property to override that default entirely (e.g. to add
`MemoryUtilization`, or to fall back to the standard 60-second resolution).

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmBackupStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```


Synthesis method to use while deploying this stack.

The Stack Synthesizer controls aspects of synthesis and deployment,
like how assets are referenced and what IAM roles to use. For more
information, see the README of the main CDK package.

If not specified, the `defaultStackSynthesizer` from `App` will be used.

`@aws-cdk/core:newStyleStackSynthesis` is set to `true` or the CDK major
version is v2. In CDK v1 `LegacyStackSynthesizer` is the default if no
other synthesizer is specified.

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmBootstrapAssetsStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```


Synthesis method to use while deploying this stack.

The Stack Synthesizer controls aspects of synthesis and deployment,
like how assets are referenced and what IAM roles to use. For more
information, see the README of the main CDK package.

If not specified, the `defaultStackSynthesizer` from `App` will be used.
If that is not specified, `DefaultStackSynthesizer` is used if
`@aws-cdk/core:newStyleStackSynthesis` is set to `true` or the CDK major
version is v2. In CDK v1 `LegacyStackSynthesizer` is the default if no
other synthesizer is specified.

A certificate to create: the primary domain, its optional subject alternative names, and the SSM parameter (in the application region) where the created ARN is published for the CloudFront stacks to read.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmCertificateRequest.Initializer"></a>

| --- | --- | --- |

| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmCertificateRequest.property.idInfix">idInfix</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Construct-id infix, unique within the stack (e.g. `Www0`, `Cdn`). |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmCertificateRequest.property.parameterName">parameterName</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Name of the SSM parameter (in `parameterRegion`) where the certificate ARN is published. |

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmCloudfrontCdnStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmCloudfrontStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `vpcOrigin`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="vpcOrigin" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmCloudfrontStackProps.property.vpcOrigin"></a>

```typescript
public readonly vpcOrigin: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Reaches the load balancer through a CloudFront VPC origin over HTTPS 443, its ARN and DNS name read from the `vpc-origin` SSM parameters published by `TmEcsStack` (the internal load balancer, or the bridge during the migration).

When false, the origin is the public load balancer's DNS name
over HTTP 80.

---

##### `vpcOriginViaBridge`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="vpcOriginViaBridge" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmCloudfrontStackProps.property.vpcOriginViaBridge"></a>

```typescript
public readonly vpcOriginViaBridge: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

The `vpc-origin` SSM parameters point at the migration bridge rather than the service load balancer (`vpcOriginBridge` without `vpcOrigin`).

CloudFront refuses to modify a VPC origin while a distribution uses it, so
each endpoint gets its own VPC origin resource: moving from the bridge to
the service load balancer creates the new VPC origin, repoints the
distribution, then deletes the old one.

---

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `synthesizer`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="synthesizer" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.synthesizer"></a>

```typescript
public readonly synthesizer: IStackSynthesizer;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.IStackSynthesizer
- *Default:* The synthesizer specified on `App`, or `DefaultStackSynthesizer` otherwise.

Synthesis method to use while deploying this stack.

The Stack Synthesizer controls aspects of synthesis and deployment,
like how assets are referenced and what IAM roles to use. For more
information, see the README of the main CDK package.

If not specified, the `defaultStackSynthesizer` from `App` will be used.
If that is not specified, `DefaultStackSynthesizer` is used if
`@aws-cdk/core:newStyleStackSynthesis` is set to `true` or the CDK major
version is v2. In CDK v1 `LegacyStackSynthesizer` is the default if no
other synthesizer is specified.

##### `tags`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="tags" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.tags"></a>


- *Type:* {[ key: string ]: string}

Tags that will be applied to the Stack.

These tags are applied to the CloudFormation Stack itself. They will not
appear in the CloudFormation template.

However, at deployment time, CloudFormation will apply these tags to all
resources in the stack that support tagging. You will not be able to exempt
resources from tagging (using the `excludeResourceTypes` property of
`Tags.of(...).add()`) for tags applied in this way.

```typescript

```

- *Type:* string[]
- *Default:* []

Variables whose value CDK generates once and stores in Secrets Manager, never in the template.

One secret is created per name; its complete ARN is
published to SSM at `/applications/<applicationName>/generated/<NAME>-arn`.
Use it for machine values no human sets (a TYPO3 encryption key, an
install-tool password).

##### `generateOriginCustomHeader`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="generateOriginCustomHeader" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.generateOriginCustomHeader"></a>

```typescript
public readonly generateOriginCustomHeader: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Generates the CloudFront origin custom-header value instead of reading it from a pre-seeded SSM parameter.

When true, this stack derives a stable,
concrete literal (identical to the one `TmCloudfrontStack` uses, since both
derive it the same way) and publishes it to
`originCustomHeaderParameterName`, so no human seeds the parameter. When
false, the value is read from the parameter (which a human must seed).

- *Default:* the task role gets no bucket access

##### `tasksInPrivateSubnets`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="tasksInPrivateSubnets" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.tasksInPrivateSubnets"></a>

```typescript
public readonly tasksInPrivateSubnets: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false - public subnets with a public IP

Runs the tasks in the private subnets with egress, without a public IP.

---

##### `vpcOrigin`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="vpcOrigin" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.vpcOrigin"></a>

```typescript
public readonly vpcOrigin: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Fronts the service with an INTERNAL load balancer meant for a CloudFront VPC origin: private subnets, HTTPS listener on 443 with an ACM certificate for `loadBalancerDomains` (DNS validation), ingress from the VPC only.

The
load balancer ARN is published in SSM for `TmCloudfrontStack`. When
false, the load balancer is public and listens on HTTP 80 for the
CloudFront origin-facing prefix list.

---

##### `vpcOriginBridge`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="vpcOriginBridge" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmEcsStackProps.property.vpcOriginBridge"></a>

```typescript
public readonly vpcOriginBridge: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Adds a second, internal HTTPS load balancer ("bridge") on the same service.

While `vpcOrigin` is false it is published as the VPC origin
endpoint, which lets CloudFront move off the public load balancer before
that one is replaced. See `CloudfrontSettings.vpcOriginBridge`.

---

```typescript
public readonly webBuildTarget: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* the Dockerfile's last stage

Docker build target stage of the `web` container.

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmPipelineStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `synthesizer`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="synthesizer" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmPipelineStackProps.property.synthesizer"></a>


- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.IStackSynthesizer
- *Default:* The synthesizer specified on `App`, or `DefaultStackSynthesizer` otherwise.

Synthesis method to use while deploying this stack.

The Stack Synthesizer controls aspects of synthesis and deployment,
like how assets are referenced and what IAM roles to use. For more
information, see the README of the main CDK package.

If not specified, the `defaultStackSynthesizer` from `App` will be used.
If that is not specified, `DefaultStackSynthesizer` is used if
`@aws-cdk/core:newStyleStackSynthesis` is set to `true` or the CDK major
version is v2. In CDK v1 `LegacyStackSynthesizer` is the default if no
other synthesizer is specified.

resources from tagging (using the `excludeResourceTypes` property of
`Tags.of(...).add()`) for tags applied in this way.

##### `end`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="end" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmRdsAuroraMysqlDashboardProps.property.end"></a>

```typescript
public readonly end: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* When the dashboard loads, the end date will be the current time.

The end of the time range to use for each widget on the dashboard when the dashboard loads.

If you specify a value for end, you must also specify a value for start.

```typescript

```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_cloudwatch.PeriodOverride
- *Default:* Auto

Use this field to specify the period for the graphs when the dashboard loads.

Specifying `Auto` causes the period of all graphs on the dashboard to automatically adapt to the time range of the dashboard.
Specifying `Inherit` ensures that the period set for each graph is always obeyed.

---

##### `start`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="start" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmRdsAuroraMysqlDashboardProps.property.start"></a>

```typescript
public readonly start: string;
```

- *Type:* string
- *Default:* When the dashboard loads, the start time will be the default time range.

The start of the time range to use for each widget on the dashboard.

You can specify start without specifying end to specify a relative time range that ends with the current time.
In this case, the value of start must begin with -P, and you can use M, H, D, W and M as abbreviations for
minutes, hours, days, weeks and months. For example, -PT8H shows the last 8 hours and -P3M shows the last three months.
You can also use start along with an end field, to specify an absolute time range.
When specifying an absolute time range, use the ISO 8601 format. For example, 2018-12-17T06:00:00.000Z.

Both properties `defaultInterval` and `start` cannot be set at once.

---

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmRdsAuroraMysqlServerlessStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmRedirectionsEc2StackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmS3StackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

version is v2. In CDK v1 `LegacyStackSynthesizer` is the default if no
other synthesizer is specified.

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmSolrStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

- *Default:* false

If true, the instance will not be able to be terminated using the Amazon EC2 console, CLI, or API.

To change this attribute after launch, use [ModifyInstanceAttribute](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_ModifyInstanceAttribute.html).
Alternatively, if you set InstanceInitiatedShutdownBehavior to terminate, you can terminate the instance
by running the shutdown command from the instance.

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-instance.html#cfn-ec2-instance-disableapitermination](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-ec2-instance.html#cfn-ec2-instance-disableapitermination)

- *Default:* false

Indicates whether the instance is optimized for Amazon EBS I/O.

This optimization provides dedicated throughput to Amazon EBS and an optimized configuration stack to provide optimal Amazon EBS I/O performance.
This optimization isn't available with all instance types.
Additional usage charges apply when using an EBS-optimized instance.

##### `enclaveEnabled`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="enclaveEnabled" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmSorlEc2Props.property.enclaveEnabled"></a>

```typescript
public readonly enclaveEnabled: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Whether the instance is enabled for AWS Nitro Enclaves.

Nitro Enclaves requires a Nitro-based virtualized parent instance with specific Intel/AMD with at least 4 vCPUs
or Graviton with at least 2 vCPUs instance types and Linux/Windows host OS,
while the enclave itself supports only Linux OS.

You can't set both `enclaveEnabled` and `hibernationEnabled` to true on the same instance.

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave.html#nitro-enclave-reqs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave.html#nitro-enclave-reqs)

You can't set both `enclaveEnabled` and `hibernationEnabled` to true on the same instance.

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-ec2-instance-hibernationoptions.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-ec2-instance-hibernationoptions.html)

```typescript
public readonly httpTokens: HttpTokens;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_ec2.HttpTokens
- *Default:* The default is conditional based on the AMI and account-level settings: - If the AMI's `ImdsSupport` is `v2.0` and the account level default is `no-preference`, the default is `HttpTokens.REQUIRED` - If the AMI's `ImdsSupport` is `v2.0` and the account level default is `V1 or V2`, the default is `HttpTokens.OPTIONAL` - See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-options.html#instance-metadata-options-order-of-precedence

The state of token usage for your instance metadata requests.

Set to 'required' to enforce IMDSv2. This is equivalent to using `requireImdsv2: true`,
but allows you to configure other metadata options alongside IMDSv2 enforcement.

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-ec2-instance-metadataoptions.html#cfn-ec2-instance-metadataoptions-httptokens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-ec2-instance-metadataoptions.html#cfn-ec2-instance-metadataoptions-httptokens)


- *Type:* boolean

configuring hop limits, or enabling instance tags), use the individual metadata option properties instead.

```typescript
public readonly role: IRole;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_iam.IRole
- *Default:* A role will automatically be created, it can be accessed via the `role` property

An IAM role to associate with the instance profile assigned to this Auto Scaling Group.

The role must be assumable by the service principal `ec2.amazonaws.com`:
Note: You can provide an instanceProfile or a role, but not both.

---

*Example*

```typescript
const role = new iam.Role(this, 'MyRole', {
  assumedBy: new iam.ServicePrincipal('ec2.amazonaws.com')
});
```

```typescript
public readonly sourceDestCheck: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* true

Specifies whether to enable an instance launched in a VPC to perform NAT.

This controls whether source/destination checking is enabled on the instance.
A value of true means that checking is enabled, and false means that checking is disabled.
The value must be false for the instance to perform NAT.

##### `ssmSessionPermissions`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="ssmSessionPermissions" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmSorlEc2Props.property.ssmSessionPermissions"></a>

```typescript
public readonly ssmSessionPermissions: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* false

Add SSM session permissions to the instance role.

Setting this to `true` adds the necessary permissions to connect
to the instance using SSM Session Manager. You can do this
from the AWS Console.

NOTE: Setting this flag to `true` may not be enough by itself.
You must also use an AMI that comes with the SSM Agent, or install
the SSM Agent yourself. See
[Working with SSM Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/ssm-agent.html)
in the SSM Developer Guide.

##### `userData`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="userData" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmSorlEc2Props.property.userData"></a>

```typescript
public readonly userData: UserData;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_ec2.UserData
- *Default:* A UserData object appropriate for the MachineImage's Operating System is created.

Specific UserData to use.

The UserData may still be mutated after creation.

---

##### `userDataCausesReplacement`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="userDataCausesReplacement" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmSorlEc2Props.property.userDataCausesReplacement"></a>

```typescript
public readonly userDataCausesReplacement: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* true if `initOptions` is specified, false otherwise.

Changes to the UserData force replacement.

Depending the EC2 instance type, changing UserData either
restarts the instance or replaces the instance.

- Instance store-backed instances are replaced.
- EBS-backed instances are restarted.

By default, restarting does not execute the new UserData so you
will need a different mechanism to ensure the instance is restarted.

Setting this to `true` will make the instance's Logical ID depend on the
UserData, which will cause CloudFormation to replace it if the UserData
changes.

---

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmVpcBaseStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

##### `synthesizer`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="synthesizer" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmVpcBaseStackProps.property.synthesizer"></a>


- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.IStackSynthesizer
- *Default:* The synthesizer specified on `App`, or `DefaultStackSynthesizer` otherwise.

Synthesis method to use while deploying this stack.

The Stack Synthesizer controls aspects of synthesis and deployment,
like how assets are referenced and what IAM roles to use. For more
information, see the README of the main CDK package.

If not specified, the `defaultStackSynthesizer` from `App` will be used.
If that is not specified, `DefaultStackSynthesizer` is used if
`@aws-cdk/core:newStyleStackSynthesis` is set to `true` or the CDK major
version is v2. In CDK v1 `LegacyStackSynthesizer` is the default if no
other synthesizer is specified.

These tags are applied to the CloudFormation Stack itself. They will not
appear in the CloudFormation template.

resources in the stack that support tagging. You will not be able to exempt
resources from tagging (using the `excludeResourceTypes` property of
`Tags.of(...).add()`) for tags applied in this way.


- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_ec2.DefaultInstanceTenancy
- *Default:* DefaultInstanceTenancy.Default (shared) tenancy

The default tenancy of instances launched into the VPC.

By setting this to dedicated tenancy, instances will be launched on
hardware dedicated to a single AWS customer, unless specifically specified

##### `enableDnsHostnames`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="enableDnsHostnames" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmVpcProps.property.enableDnsHostnames"></a>

```typescript
public readonly enableDnsHostnames: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* true

Indicates whether the instances launched in the VPC get public DNS hostnames.

If this attribute is true, instances in the VPC get public DNS hostnames,
but only if the enableDnsSupport attribute is also set to true.

---

##### `enableDnsSupport`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="enableDnsSupport" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmVpcProps.property.enableDnsSupport"></a>

```typescript
public readonly enableDnsSupport: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean
- *Default:* true

Indicates whether the DNS resolution is supported for the VPC.

If this attribute is false, the Amazon-provided DNS server in the VPC that
resolves public DNS hostnames to IP addresses is not enabled. If this
attribute is true, queries to the Amazon provided DNS server at the
169.254.169.253 IP address, or the reserved IP address at the base of the
VPC IPv4 network range plus two will succeed.

---

Note this is specific to IPv6 addresses.

---

##### `maxAzs`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="maxAzs" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmVpcProps.property.maxAzs"></a>

```typescript
public readonly maxAzs: number;
```

- *Type:* number
- *Default:* 3

Define the maximum number of AZs to use in this region.

If the region has more AZs than you want to use (for example, because of
EIP limits), pick a lower number here. The AZs will be sorted and picked
from the start of the list.

If you pick a higher number than the number of AZs in the region, all AZs
in the region will be selected. To use "all AZs" available to your
account, use a high number (such as 99).

Be aware that environment-agnostic stacks will be created with access to
only 2 AZs, so to use more than 2 AZs, be sure to specify the account and
region on your stack.

Specify this option only if you do not specify `availabilityZones`.

---


- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_ec2.NatProvider
- *Default:* NatProvider.gateway()

Select between NAT gateways or NAT instances. NAT gateways
may not be available in all AWS regions.

---

##### `natGateways`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="natGateways" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmVpcProps.property.natGateways"></a>

```typescript

```

- *Type:* number
- *Default:* One NAT gateway/instance per Availability Zone

The number of NAT Gateways/Instances to create.

The type of NAT gateway or instance will be determined by the
`natGatewayProvider` parameter.

You can set this number lower than the number of Availability Zones in your
VPC in order to save on NAT cost. Be aware you may be charged for
cross-AZ data traffic instead.

---

Configures the subnets which will have NAT Gateways/Instances.

You can pick a specific group of subnets by specifying the group name;
the picked subnets must be public subnets.

Only necessary if you have more than one public subnet group.


- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.aws_ec2.SubnetConfiguration[]
- *Default:* The VPC CIDR will be evenly divided between 1 public and 1 private subnet per AZ.

Configure the subnets to build for each AZ.

Each entry in this list configures a Subnet Group; each group will contain a
subnet for each Availability Zone.

For example, if you want 1 public subnet, 1 private subnet, and 1 isolated
subnet in each AZ provide the following:

```ts
new ec2.Vpc(this, 'VPC', {
  subnetConfiguration: [
     {
       cidrMask: 24,
       name: 'ingress',
       subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PUBLIC,
     },
     {
       cidrMask: 24,
       name: 'application',
       subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS,
     },
     {
       cidrMask: 28,
       name: 'rds',
       subnetType: ec2.SubnetType.PRIVATE_ISOLATED,
     }
  ]
});
```

##### `env`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="env" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmWafStackProps.property.env"></a>

```typescript
public readonly env: Environment;
```

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.Environment
- *Default:* The environment of the containing `Stage` if available, otherwise create the stack will be environment-agnostic.

The AWS environment (account/region) where this stack will be deployed.

Set the `region`/`account` fields of `env` to either a concrete value to
select the indicated environment (recommended for production stacks), or to
the values of environment variables
`CDK_DEFAULT_REGION`/`CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` to let the target environment
depend on the AWS credentials/configuration that the CDK CLI is executed
under (recommended for development stacks).

If the `Stack` is instantiated inside a `Stage`, any undefined
`region`/`account` fields from `env` will default to the same field on the
encompassing `Stage`, if configured there.

If either `region` or `account` are not set nor inherited from `Stage`, the
Stack will be considered "*environment-agnostic*"". Environment-agnostic
stacks can be deployed to any environment but may not be able to take
advantage of all features of the CDK. For example, they will not be able to
use environmental context lookups such as `ec2.Vpc.fromLookup` and will not
automatically translate Service Principals to the right format based on the
environment's AWS partition, and other such enhancements.

---

*Example*

```typescript
// Use a concrete account and region to deploy this stack to:
// `.account` and `.region` will simply return these values.
new Stack(app, 'Stack1', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  },
});

// Use the CLI's current credentials to determine the target environment:
// `.account` and `.region` will reflect the account+region the CLI
// is configured to use (based on the user CLI credentials)
new Stack(app, 'Stack2', {
  env: {
    account: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT,
    region: process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_REGION
  },
});

// Define multiple stacks stage associated with an environment
const myStage = new Stage(app, 'MyStage', {
  env: {
    account: '123456789012',
    region: 'us-east-1'
  }
});

// both of these stacks will use the stage's account/region:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to the concrete values as above
new MyStack(myStage, 'Stack1');
new YourStack(myStage, 'Stack2');

// Define an environment-agnostic stack:
// `.account` and `.region` will resolve to `{ "Ref": "AWS::AccountId" }` and `{ "Ref": "AWS::Region" }` respectively.
// which will only resolve to actual values by CloudFormation during deployment.
new MyStack(app, 'Stack1');
```

- *Default:* no permissions boundary is applied

Options for applying a permissions boundary to all IAM Roles and Users created within this Stage.

Be aware that this feature uses Aspects, and the Aspects are applied at the
Stack level with a priority of `MUTATING` (if the feature flag
`@aws-cdk/core:aspectPrioritiesMutating` is set) or `DEFAULT` (if the flag
is not set). This is relevant if you are both using your own Aspects to
assign Permissions Boundaries, as well as specifying this property.  The
Aspect added by this property will overwrite the Permissions Boundary
assigned by your own Aspect if both: (a) your Aspect has a lower or equal
priority to the automatic Aspect, and (b) your Aspect is applied *above*
the Stack level.  If either of those conditions are not true, your own
Aspect will win.

We recommend assigning Permissions Boundaries only using the provided APIs,
and not using custom Aspects.

### WafSettings <a name="WafSettings" id="tm-cdk-constructs.WafSettings"></a>

Baseline WebACL associated with the distributions.

It is created in
us-east-1, as CloudFront requires.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="tm-cdk-constructs.WafSettings.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { WafSettings } from 'tm-cdk-constructs'

const wafSettings: WafSettings = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.WafSettings.property.blockedCountryCodes">blockedCountryCodes</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | Country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) whose requests are blocked. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.WafSettings.property.logging">logging</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Sends WebACL logs to CloudWatch Logs (30-day retention). |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.WafSettings.property.protectCdn">protectCdn</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Associates the WebACL with the CDN distribution too. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.WafSettings.property.rateLimit">rateLimit</a></code> | <code>number</code> | Maximum requests per client IP in any 5-minute window. |

### TmParameterNames <a name="TmParameterNames" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames"></a>

Names of the SSM parameters the package creates and reads.

Convention: `/tm/<env>/<component>/<resource>/<attribute>`, lower-kebab-case,
e.g. `/tm/prod/rds/cluster/writer-endpoint`. `<env>` is the
`environmentName` of the environment parameters.

Producer stacks write these parameters and consumer stacks read them at
deploy time, so no stack imports another stack's CloudFormation exports.

#### Initializers <a name="Initializers" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { TmParameterNames } from 'tm-cdk-constructs'

new TmParameterNames()
```

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |

---


#### Static Functions <a name="Static Functions" id="Static Functions"></a>

| **Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.bastionSecurityGroupId">bastionSecurityGroupId</a></code> | Bastion security group ID. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.bootstrapAssetsBucketName">bootstrapAssetsBucketName</a></code> | Name of the pipeline-level bootstrap-assets bucket, holding the database dump (`db/latest.sql`) and any future seed asset. Published by `TmBootstrapAssetsStack` and read by the RDS bootstrap construct. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontBasicAuth">cloudfrontBasicAuth</a></code> | Default name of the hand-made parameter holding the base64 `user:password` of the www basic authentication. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontCdnCertificateArn">cloudfrontCdnCertificateArn</a></code> | Default name of the hand-made parameter holding the ACM certificate ARN (us-east-1) of the CDN distribution. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontCdnDistributionId">cloudfrontCdnDistributionId</a></code> | ID of the CDN distribution. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontDistributionIds">cloudfrontDistributionIds</a></code> | Default name of the distribution-ID parameter read by tm_cloudfront and the pipeline invalidation step. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontOriginCustomHeader">cloudfrontOriginCustomHeader</a></code> | Default name of the hand-made parameter holding the secret header value that CloudFront sends to the load balancer (`X-Custom-Header`). |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontWwwCertificateArn">cloudfrontWwwCertificateArn</a></code> | Default name of the hand-made parameter holding the ACM certificate ARN (us-east-1) of a www distribution. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.cloudfrontWwwDistributionId">cloudfrontWwwDistributionId</a></code> | ID of a www distribution. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.ecsLoadBalancerDnsName">ecsLoadBalancerDnsName</a></code> | DNS name of the application load balancer. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.ecsVpcOriginLoadBalancerArn">ecsVpcOriginLoadBalancerArn</a></code> | ARN of the load balancer CloudFront reaches through its VPC origin: the bridge while it is the endpoint, otherwise the service's own. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.ecsVpcOriginLoadBalancerDnsName">ecsVpcOriginLoadBalancerDnsName</a></code> | DNS name of the load balancer behind the VPC origin (see `ecsVpcOriginLoadBalancerArn`). |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.generatedSecretArn">generatedSecretArn</a></code> | SSM parameter holding the complete ARN of a CDK-generated application secret. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.of">of</a></code> | Builds a parameter name that follows the convention. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.rdsClusterArn">rdsClusterArn</a></code> | RDS cluster ARN. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.rdsReaderEndpoint">rdsReaderEndpoint</a></code> | RDS cluster reader endpoint hostname. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.rdsSecurityGroupId">rdsSecurityGroupId</a></code> | RDS cluster security group ID. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.rdsWriterEndpoint">rdsWriterEndpoint</a></code> | RDS cluster writer endpoint hostname. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.redirectionsPublicIp">redirectionsPublicIp</a></code> | Public IP (Elastic IP) of the redirection instance. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.redisPrimaryEndpoint">redisPrimaryEndpoint</a></code> | Redis primary endpoint hostname. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.redisSecurityGroupId">redisSecurityGroupId</a></code> | Redis security group ID. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.s3ContentBucketName">s3ContentBucketName</a></code> | FAL content bucket name. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.s3ErrorBucketName">s3ErrorBucketName</a></code> | CloudFront error page bucket name. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.s3LogBucketName">s3LogBucketName</a></code> | CloudFront access log bucket name. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.serviceUserCredentialsSecretArn">serviceUserCredentialsSecretArn</a></code> | ARN of the Secrets Manager secret holding a service user's access key (`AccessKeyId` and `SecretAccessKey` fields). |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.solrSecurityGroupId">solrSecurityGroupId</a></code> | Solr security group ID. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.solrWriterEndpoint">solrWriterEndpoint</a></code> | Solr writer endpoint hostname. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.solrWriterPort">solrWriterPort</a></code> | Solr writer port. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.vpcHostedZoneId">vpcHostedZoneId</a></code> | Private hosted zone ID attached to the VPC. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.vpcId">vpcId</a></code> | VPC ID. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.vpcIsolatedSubnetIds">vpcIsolatedSubnetIds</a></code> | Comma-separated isolated subnet IDs, in availability-zone order. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.vpcPrivateSubnetIds">vpcPrivateSubnetIds</a></code> | Comma-separated private (with egress) subnet IDs, in availability-zone order. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.vpcPublicSubnetIds">vpcPublicSubnetIds</a></code> | Comma-separated public subnet IDs, in availability-zone order. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.wafWebAclArn">wafWebAclArn</a></code> | ARN of the CloudFront-scope WebACL, written in the application region. |

---

##### `generatedSecretArn` <a name="generatedSecretArn" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.generatedSecretArn"></a>

```typescript
import { TmParameterNames } from 'tm-cdk-constructs'

TmParameterNames.generatedSecretArn(applicationName: string, name: string)
```

SSM parameter holding the complete ARN of a CDK-generated application secret.

The generated-secrets path (`TmEcsStack.buildSecrets`) publishes
every generated secret's ARN here, under the application namespace rather
than the `/tm/...` one. It is the single source of truth both ECS and the
RDS bootstrap read for a shared generated secret such as
`TM_DATABASE_PASSWORD`.

###### `applicationName`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="applicationName" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.generatedSecretArn.parameter.applicationName"></a>

- *Type:* string

the ECS `applicationName` (secrets path segment).

---

###### `name`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="name" id="tm-cdk-constructs.TmParameterNames.generatedSecretArn.parameter.name"></a>

- *Type:* string

the variable name, e.g. `TM_DATABASE_PASSWORD`.

---

### FalS3Driver <a name="FalS3Driver" id="tm-cdk-constructs.FalS3Driver"></a>

TYPO3 extension reading the FAL content bucket.

Selects the variable names
the stage passes to the containers.

#### Members <a name="Members" id="Members"></a>

| **Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.FalS3Driver.TM_S3ASSETS">TM_S3ASSETS</a></code> | tm_s3assets (deprecated): `TM_S3ASSETS_BUCKET_NAME`, `TM_S3ASSETS_REGION`, `TM_S3ASSETS_DOMAIN` (the CDN domain), and with the S3 service user `TM_S3ASSETS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `TM_S3ASSETS_SECRET_KEY`. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.FalS3Driver.AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3">AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3</a></code> | aus_driver_amazon_s3: `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_BUCKET`, `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_REGION`, `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (the CDN domain, without protocol), and with the S3 service user `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_KEY` / `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_SECRET`. |

---

##### `TM_S3ASSETS` <a name="TM_S3ASSETS" id="tm-cdk-constructs.FalS3Driver.TM_S3ASSETS"></a>

tm_s3assets (deprecated): `TM_S3ASSETS_BUCKET_NAME`, `TM_S3ASSETS_REGION`, `TM_S3ASSETS_DOMAIN` (the CDN domain), and with the S3 service user `TM_S3ASSETS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `TM_S3ASSETS_SECRET_KEY`.

---


##### `AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3` <a name="AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3" id="tm-cdk-constructs.FalS3Driver.AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3"></a>

aus_driver_amazon_s3: `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_BUCKET`, `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_REGION`, `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (the CDN domain, without protocol), and with the S3 service user `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_KEY` / `TM_AUS_DRIVER_AMAZON_S3_SECRET`.

Without
the service user the key variables are not set and the driver falls back
to the AWS SDK default credential chain, i.e. the ECS task role, which the
stage then grants read/write on the content bucket.

---

### PipelineSourceType <a name="PipelineSourceType" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSourceType"></a>

Where `TmPipelineStack` reads its infrastructure and application source from.

A string-literal union (`'codecommit' | 's3'`) cannot be used here: jsii does
not support TypeScript literal unions in the public API, so the selector is
an enum.

#### Members <a name="Members" id="Members"></a>

| **Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSourceType.CODECOMMIT">CODECOMMIT</a></code> | CodeCommit repositories, polled through CodeStar connections. |
| <code><a href="#tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSourceType.S3">S3</a></code> | Versioned S3 buckets fed by GitHub Actions over OIDC, each change detected by an EventBridge rule. |

---

##### `CODECOMMIT` <a name="CODECOMMIT" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSourceType.CODECOMMIT"></a>

CodeCommit repositories, polled through CodeStar connections.

The library's
original and default behaviour.

---


##### `S3` <a name="S3" id="tm-cdk-constructs.PipelineSourceType.S3"></a>

Versioned S3 buckets fed by GitHub Actions over OIDC, each change detected by an EventBridge rule.

No CodeCommit mirror needed.

---
